Updated  - November 01, 2026 05:30 am IST - New York

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani. File.
                                          | Photo Credit: AP

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has claimed in a social media post that President Donald Trump has agreed to grant a visa to the mother of a 15-year-old immigrant from Ghana who was shot dead earlier this week.

The White House did not immediately respond to an e-mail from The Associated Press confirming the administration would be issuing the visa.

The teen, Javits Frimpong, was on his way to school in a Bronx neighbourhood shortly before 9.30 a.m. on Thursday (October 29, 2026) when he was shot in the abdomen, New York City police said. He was pronounced dead at a hospital later that day. No arrests have yet been made, and the killing remains under investigation.

“The murder of a child is a pain no parent should have to endure, let alone from thousands of miles away,” Mr. Mamdani wrote on Saturday (October 31, 2026) on X. “Javits Frimpong's mother deserves to say goodbye to her son in person. I just got off the phone with President Trump, and he has agreed to grant her visa immediately.”

“All of New York City is mourning this tragedy,” he said.

Frimpong arrived in the Bronx from Ghana a year ago to be with his father and begin a new life in the United States, according to U.S. Rep. Ritchie Torres, a Democrat from the Bronx.

Frimpong was on his way to school when he was shot, Torres wrote on X.

“Our entire borough is mourning a young man who should have had his whole future ahead of him,” Mr. Torres said. “Every child in the Bronx deserves to walk to school without fearing for their life, and no parent should ever have to endure what Javits's father, Thomas, is enduring now.”

Foreign Minister Sam Okudzeto Ablakwa said in a post on X that Ghanaian officials in New York are coordinating with local authorities and that the Foreign Ministry “will work tirelessly with U.S. authorities to ensure justice is secured.”

Mr. Trump has clamped down on immigration during his second term, including suspending the processing of visas from 75 countries.

Carlos Barajas Ramirez, 18, was arrested on suspicion of publishing threats to commit a shooting at Hollister High School.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

An 18-year-old has been arrested after detectives uncovered his alleged plot to shoot up a California high school.

Carlos Barajas Ramirez was arrested at his home in Hollister and booked into the San Benito County Jail on suspicion of publishing threats to commit a school shooting at Hollister High School, according to the Hollister Police department.

The alarm was first raised on September 27 when the Northern California Regional Intelligence Centre alerted Hollister police to reports of an individual attempting to buy a firearm and planning an attack at the high school.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Never miss a story

Working with the FBI, detectives traced the suspect’s digital trail after learning he had shared operational plans and “radical ideation” with others online.

Investigators interviewed witnesses who had been in contact with the suspect, uncovering messages detailing an alleged mass shooting plot before using account metadata to identify Barajas Ramirez and his location.

California Post News: Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X, YouTube, WhatsApp, LinkedInCalifornia Post Sports Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, XCalifornia Post  Opinion California Post Newsletters: Sign up here!California Post App: Download here!Home delivery: Sign up here!Page Six Hollywood: Sign up here!

Detectives and officers subsequently went to Ramirez’s home on October 13, where an interview and investigation determined he had actively planned to carry out the attack.

Police have not stated whether Ramirez had obtained a firearm prior to his arrest or whether he had direct ties to the school.

The department acknowledged it had collaborated quietly with school administrators throughout the probe to avoid alerting the suspect or jeopardizing community safety.

Dr Shawn Tennenbaum, superintendent of the San Benito High School District, praised the police intervention, noting that rapid guidance from law enforcement had been “instrumental to ensuring a safe environment for all”.

Authorities have said there is no active danger to students or staff.
